The dataset was collected from 20 wind turbines across two wind farms located 700 km apart.
The dataset contained 15-16 days of data, with some days having icing events.
The dataset was split into 60% training and 40% testing.
Three imbalance ratios were tested: 20:1, 50:1, and 100:1 (non-icing to icing samples).
FedHPb outperformed the second-best method, BiFL, by an average of 19.64% in F-beta score and 5.73% in balanced accuracy across the three imbalance ratios.
Even at the highest imbalance ratio of 100:1, FedHPb maintained high F-beta (73.08%) and balanced accuracy (85.35%) scores.
The client-side LCNN model uses LSTM for time-series feature extraction, followed by a CNN module with attention, normalization, and activation layers.
The FedHPb server aggregates class prototypes from clients by calculating a weighted average, with weights based on the size of each client's label dataset.
The main evaluation metrics used were F-beta score (with beta=2) and balanced accuracy.
FedHPb's prototype-based approach handled data heterogeneity better than gradient-based communication used in other FL methods.
FedHPb's contrastive supervised loss function improved classification of minority icing events compared to standard FL and class imbalance techniques.
The wind turbine data exhibited significant heterogeneity due to differences in geographical locations, operating environments, and hardware configurations.
Icing events on wind turbine blades can decrease global annual power generation by nearly 30%.
Traditional centralized training methods for blade icing detection raise serious privacy concerns.
Traditional federated learning methods are still limited in addressing data heterogeneity and class imbalance issues in wind turbine data.
